candidates.change_summary: Replace `owner = newOwner;` with `owner = address(0);` to set owner to zero address regardless of argument.
Replace `owner = newOwner;` with `owner = msg.sender;` to retain current owner instead of transferring.
Replace `require(msg.sender == owner);` with `require(true);` to remove the sender check, allowing anyone to change owner.
Delete the `require(msg.sender == owner);` statement so the modifier imposes no restriction.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from owned() so it can be called by anyone, changing owner state before the call.
Replace the onlyOwner modifier with a revert statement so owned() always fails, altering the observable outcome when called after a transfer.
Insert an assignment `owner = address(0);` inside owned() so the call changes owner to zero address.
Replace the empty body of owned() with `owner = address(0);` so owner is cleared on a successful call.
Replace the empty body of owned() with `owner = msg.sender;` so owner is overwritten to the caller.
Replace the require condition with `true` so the onlyOwner modifier always passes, allowing any caller to execute owned() and potentially change state first.
Replace the require condition with `false` so the onlyOwner modifier always reverts, preventing owned() from ever completing normally.
Delete the entire require statement so onlyOwner becomes an empty modifier, removing access control from owned().
Remove the require check in the onlyOwner modifier so anyone can call transferOwnership.
Change the require condition to always fail, preventing any transfer of ownership.
Change the body of transferOwnership to set owner to a constant address instead of the parameter.
Change the body of transferOwnership to set owner to msg.sender instead of newOwner.
Delete the assignment, so owner is never updated by transferOwnership.
